source.scope: Published infinite-plane polar stress equations for remote y-axis loading only. This repository authors its own finite exact-restriction problem, calculations and text. The source's uniform finite-edge FE example is not an exact finite-boundary reference.

model: Homogeneous, isotropic, linear-elastic infinitesimal plane stress, no body force, no initial stress, no thermal strain
geometry: Quarter domain 0<=x<=B, 0<=y<=B, x^2+y^2>=a^2; circular traction-free hole centered at origin; unit-thickness in-plane stress balance

boundary_conditions.hole: zero traction at r=a, outward normal -e_r
boundary_conditions.right: full nonuniform Kirsch traction sigma(x=B,y) dot (1,0), including shear
boundary_conditions.top: full nonuniform Kirsch traction sigma(x,y=B) dot (0,1), including shear
boundary_conditions.left_symmetry: u_x=0 at x=0, a<=y<=B; tangential traction is zero
boundary_conditions.bottom_symmetry: u_y=0 at y=0, a<=x<=B; tangential traction is zero
boundary_conditions.rigid_modes: The two intersecting symmetry constraints exclude both translations and in-plane rotation; the origin itself is removed by the hole

loading: Remote positive sigma is tension along +y; theta=atan2(y,x) is measured counterclockwise from +x. Positive sigma_xy follows traction t=sigma dot n. The y-loaded Kirsch source convention is used without rotating its angle.

claim.artifact_class: exact analytic reference and separately differentiated Airy potential evaluated in binary64
claim.decision_error: No physical/application acceptance error is set. Numerical comparison budget below is only for reference-route reproduction.

budgets.note: Inclusive numerical reproduction gates only. No FE approximation or engineering allowable. No tolerance inferred from a rounded published target.

hypotheses: Polar Kirsch and independent Airy second derivatives agree at every registered sample
Hole and symmetry tractions vanish within numerical gates
All four quarter-domain boundary tractions close net force and moment at the registered quadrature levels
Divergence and plane-stress compatibility residuals fit prospective finite-difference gates
exposure: Public development only; no frozen labels, reserved cases, FE host run, pilot or policy tuning
